General

Contoso designs, builds and sells cloud platforms, productivity software and devices to consumers, small businesses and large enterprises in more than one hundred countries.

Our mission is to help every organisation run its operations on reliable infrastructure, and we invest continuously in data centres, networking equipment and custom silicon to meet that demand.

Competition

The markets for our products are highly competitive, and our competitors range from large diversified technology companies to small specialised firms with a single product line.

ITEM 1A.RISK FACTORS

Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including those described below, which could harm our business, reputation, financial condition and operating results.

Risks Specific to our Company

Our increasing investment in new businesses, products, services and technologies is inherently risky, and could divert management attention and harm our financial condition and operating results.

To meet the compute capacity demands of model training and inference, we commit years in advance to land, power and servers, and we may have excess capacity that we cannot easily redeploy if demand develops more slowly than we expect.
---
Supply constraints on graphics processors, memory and power equipment may delay the opening of new data centres and limit the revenue we can recognise from capacity sold in advance.

Risks Related to Financing

We have issued senior unsecured notes and may issue more debt in the future, which could limit our flexibility in planning for or reacting to changes in our business and industry.

Changes in interest rates could increase the cost of our borrowings and reduce the fair value of the fixed income securities held in our investment portfolio.

| Item 7. | | | Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations | | |

Forward-Looking Statements

This Annual Report on Form 10-K includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, and actual results could differ materially from those anticipated.

Overview

Net sales increased in every segment during the year, driven by cloud services consumption, higher subscription revenue and a recovery in device unit sales in the second half.

| Year Ended December 31, | 2024 | 2025 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Net sales | 512,300 | 588,900 |
| Operating income | 61,400 | 74,800 |
| Purchases of property and equipment | (83,000) | (121,500) |

Capital expenditures rose sharply as we added data centre capacity for artificial intelligence workloads, and we expect them to keep increasing next year.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

Cash provided by operating activities funded most of our capital expenditures, and we also drew on commercial paper and the proceeds of a new bond issuance.
